payload.claim: `build` runs four separate top-level queries (lines 124, 136, 146, 171) on the same connection with no explicit `BEGIN`, so sqlite3 gives each its own implicit read transaction rather than one snapshot across the whole call. Since this module exists to state the run record 'as it stands right now' for `saffron serve` while a batch is concurrently writing to the same ledger file (per the module docstring and ADR 9), a commit landing between two of these queries can produce a torn read: e.g. a task created after the tasks query (line 146) runs will have attempts that pass the `task_nodes.get(...)` check at line 172 as `None` and be silently dropped with no `LeftOut` entry, unlike the explicit `unknown_state`/`unknown_risk` exclusions the module otherwise records. The concurrency test added (`test_build_reads_a_ledger_another_connection_is_writing`) only exercises a single already-committed write held constant through the whole call, so it cannot catch this cross-query inconsistency.
